sources.primaryDocumentTitle: Rahmenlehrplan für die Jahrgangsstufen 1-10 der Berliner und Brandenburger Schulen, Teil C Biologie, Jahrgangsstufen 7-10, 2015
sources.scope: Sek I; topic 3.4 grades7/8; topic 3.6 grades9/10
sources.primaryEvidenceParaphrase: The overview places endocrine/puberty content in 7/8 and nervous-system content in 9/10. Topic3.4 concerns puberty, sexual hormones and cycle regulation. Topic3.6 concerns sensory organs, neuron form/function, nervous-system organisation, addiction prevention; synapse is a named term. It permits different abstraction levels for information transfer and models. Stress prevention is a possible context, not a required chronic endocrine feedback mechanism.

sources.primaryDocumentTitle: Bildungsplan Gymnasium Sekundarstufe I: Biologie, Hamburg 2011
sources.scope: Sek I; distinguish year8 minimum from transition-to-Studienstufe minimum
sources.primaryEvidenceParaphrase: The table separates describing neuron/brain/spinal-cord form and function at year8 from explaining this at transition. Both columns retain conduction and reflexes. The transition column explicitly compares hormonal and nervous systems. The health communication table covers drug effects on the nervous system. Those clauses do not state electrical synapses, receptor-potential categories or chronic hormonal stress feedback.
sources.liveRetrievalBoundary: official 2011 PDF accessible; current cohort applicability of the 2011 edition was not separately established

sources.primaryDocumentTitle: Rahmenplan für den Sekundarbereich I Gymnasium/Gesamtschule Biologie, Mecklenburg-Vorpommern 2022
sources.scope: Sek I grade 8; nervous-system teaching block
sources.primaryEvidenceParaphrase: The mandatory block names neuron form/function, excitation transfer and central nervous system. Model use is an instruction; a competency example describes neuron structure with a model and explains transfer using applications. Learning/memory appears as a contextual suggestion for brain function. Neither electrical-synapse mechanism nor quantitative action-potential analysis is named here.
sources.liveRetrievalBoundary: official PDF accessible; byte identity to retained local PDF was not checked

sources.primaryDocumentTitle: Kernlehrplan für die Sekundarstufe I Gymnasium in Nordrhein-Westfalen: Biologie, Heft 3413, 2019
sources.scope: Sek I; IF3 first-stage expectations, IF7/IF8 end-of-Sek I expectations
sources.primaryEvidenceParaphrase: IF3 covers puberty, organs and a basic cycle explanation. IF7 explicitly uses simple neuron/synapse models, describes chemical-synapse transfer through a simple model, compares neural and hormonal transfer, explains bodily stress reactions and uses negative feedback/opposing hormones for blood glucose. IF8 covers hormonal cycle regulation and data-based cycle explanation. Electrical synapses, primary/secondary receptor categories and chronic stress feedback are not named in these clauses.
sources.liveRetrievalBoundary: official PDF accessible; byte identity to retained local PDF was not checked

sources.primaryDocumentTitle: Lehrplan Naturwissenschaftliche Fächer Biologie, Chemie, Physik Klassenstufen 7-10 Rheinland-Pfalz 2014
sources.scope: Sek I grades7–10 thematic field7; no official GK/LK distinction in this clause
sources.primaryEvidenceParaphrase: TF7 requires investigating sensory-organ function, deriving sensory-organ and neuron structure/function through models or model experiments, and applying the lock/key model of synaptic transfer to several problem settings, including poisons/drugs. Its concept list identifies the chemical synapse. Source-extraction goal003 omits the several-problems qualifier, and both affected sourceRefs incorrectly cite printed 35 instead of36.

sources.primaryDocumentTitle: Fachanforderungen Biologie: Allgemein bildende Schulen, Sekundarstufe I, Sekundarstufe II, 3. überarbeitete Auflage 2023
sources.scope: 2023 edition, Sek I grades7–9(10), only applicable outgoing cohorts after new2026 phase-in
sources.primaryEvidenceParaphrase: SR4 describes/explains nervous-system constituents and functions, including neurons, somatic/vegetative systems and brain; endocrine-system constituents/functions remain a separate competency. IK4 describes communication on cellular, organ and organism levels; hormone, nervous and immune systems are listed on organ level. These clauses do not name synapse mechanisms or explicitly require a combined neuroendocrine circuit.
sources.liveRetrievalBoundary: official Fachportal says the 2026 Sek I edition starts progressively with 2026/27 entry years and 2023 remains for outgoing cohorts; the 2026 content itself was not reviewed

sources.primaryEvidenceParaphrase: LB1 requires knowing nervous-system form/function, neuron/synapse conduction/transfer, with electrical impulses and transmitter substances as explanatory notes. It then covers hormone-system overview and regulation, explicitly including combined nerve/hormone action and pituitary; transfer of a biological regulatory circuit to blood glucose is a distinct operator. Electrical impulses do not mean electrical synapses. Introductory, knowledge, application and judgement operators must remain distinct.
sources.liveRetrievalBoundary: official2025 PDF accessible; byte identity to retained local PDF was not checked

sources.scope: Sek I grade 9; human/environment competency focus
sources.primaryEvidenceParaphrase: The source compares nervous-system form/function/complexity, explains human brain information processing and drug impairment, describes combined nervous/hormonal control, and names their interaction in stress. It separately includes stress prevention, risk judgement and sensory-organ/behaviour experiments. These grade 9 pages do not specify neuron-cell morphology or synapse mechanisms; later upper-secondary pages cannot substitute for this stage.
sources.liveRetrievalBoundary: official PDF accessible; byte identity to retained local PDF was not checked

sources.primaryDocumentTitle: Thueringer Lehrplan Biologie fuer den Erwerb der allgemeinen Hochschulreife 2024
sources.scope: Sek I grades7/8; human biology section
sources.primaryEvidenceParaphrase: The nervous section describes neuron parts and names its function, depicts the sensory–central–motor chain and requires showing strengthened/deactivated neural connections as a basis for learning. Hormonal puberty/cycle content and insulin/glucagon regulation are separate clauses. The assigned lower section does not name chemical/electrical synapse mechanisms or combined neuroendocrine circuits. Upper-course clauses later in the same PDF are separate.
